turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hey, good to have you here. How are you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is there any bread that isn't stale, Owen?

turns.speaker: other
turns.text: There's a loaf in the freezer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, next thing. I'm working in the office three days a week again, and I need to sort out my dog during the day.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've got a few options here and I want to get through all of them before you say anything.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a doggy daycare near work, he'd play with other dogs all day, but it's pricey and he can be shy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A dog walker could come at lunch for an hour, much cheaper, but he'd be home alone the rest of the time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or my retired neighbour offered to have him at her place, free, though she's not that strong on a lead.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's all the options I've got, Moshi. Be honest, which is best?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If he's shy, a whole day at daycare might be a lot for him at first. The lunchtime walker is a good middle ground if he's okay napping alone. The neighbour is lovely and free, but a strong puller and a not so strong walker is a worry.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a fine age with some supervision. A big cage, a wheel and a deep layer of bedding are the essentials.
